sentences.text: Petitioner has further prayed for initiating action against the Respondent No. 9-Arsu Tudu, constable, Jamshedpur for lodging false case of rape against the petitioner.
Petitioner has also prayed for adequate compensation.

2. It appears that the Respondent No. 9 has instituted a case against the petitioner vide Sidhgora P.S. Case No. 116 of 2020 under section 376(2)(i) of the Indian Penal Code and section 3(2)(v) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, alleging therein that on 20.08.2020 at about 6.30 p.m., petitioner had raped her.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Police after the investigation, has submitted charge sheet against the petitioner.
Petitioner faced trial in SC/ST Case No. 29 of 2020 arising out of Sidhgora P.S. Case No. 116 of 2020.
Respondent No. 9 in her deposition has given complete go-bye to the prosecution case and stated that the petitioner has established sexual relationship with her with her consent.
She has also stated that the petitioner has not raped her.
In view of her statement, petitioner was acquitted of the charges.
3. Now, the petitioner has filed this writ application with the aforesaid prayers.
Petitioner is claiming that the he has been falsely implicated in this case by the Respondent No. 9 in connivance with some police officials of his department.
4. Petitioner can invoke an alternative remedy by filing a case before the competent court against the Respondent No. 9 for instituting a false case against him.
Petitioner can also seek damage, if the Respondent No. 9 is found to have instituted false case against him.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner may be given liberty to agitate his grievances before the competent court.
6. In view of the aforesaid facts, this writ application is dismissed with liberty to the petitioner to approach the competent court.
